title: The Great Divergence
summary: The Great Divergence is the rise of the gap in incomes between the West and the rest. Pomeranz put the term into scholarly use in 2000, arguing that the gap began with the Industrial Revolution and modern growth in Britain. Broadberry and Gupta answered, from wage evidence, that it was already well underway before 1800. The gap has narrowed since rapid growth in China, India and other regions from the 1980s, known as the Great Convergence.

where.modern_name: Worldwide; stand-in pin at London, United Kingdom

importance.justification: The gap set the modern distribution of wealth between world regions.

related.because: Fossil-fuelled mechanization and factory production provided the technological leap that drove Western economies ahead of agrarian economies.
